| D-266 | **Scan enhancement becomes shadow removal + deskew + automatic color or grayscale, black-and-white uses a local threshold; searchable PDFs can write Chinese, Japanese and Korean text** (supersedes D-078's color matrix and P-028's "write Latin letters only"): `scan.enhance` first scales the page to 800 on the long side for analysis (`planScanEnhance` of `@morph/tool-image`, pure TS, testable in Node): in each cell (48 cells on the long side) the brightest 10% of pixels are taken as the paper color, cells more than half darker than the median of their surroundings are treated as a picture or black block and filled in from the surroundings (so they are not pulled to white; the median is used so that no dark ring appears beside a glare), each channel is estimated separately, and after dividing by the paper the paper is neutral white; the black point is the darkest 0.5% and the white point is 94% of the paper color; the projection method finds text skew within ±7°, and no rotation is made when unsure or below 0.15°; "Auto", after the background is divided out, looks at color per 4×4 block, and keeps color only if the blocks with strong color exceed 0.1%, otherwise outputs grayscale; in color mode pixels close to gray lose their color (suppressing moiré and the colored fringes of noise); color and grayscale darken the midtones a little (γ 1.3), so faint text is clearer. | D-272 | **Scan to Excel (phase 1)**: the new action `ocr.toExcel` (image → xlsx, part of the text recognition tool), with the parameters `lang` (same as "Recognize text", default `auto` and not asked, D-278; when auto picks a language that the device cannot recognize, it reports `tableUnsupported`) and `scope` (`all` for all content, the default; `tables` for table content only); multiple pages produce one xlsx with one worksheet per page ("Page N"). It recognizes only tables with lines: the new package `@morph/tool-office` (pure TS) uses Sauvola binarization to find long dark runs by row and by column (a gap of 3 pixels is allowed, at least max(24 pixels, 1.5% of the page width), and a run thicker than 1.5% of the page is a color block; a "horizontal line" that falls in the middle of a recognition box is a bold character and is removed), lines broken at the same position by no more than max(8 pixels, 0.5%) are joined into one line, and only lines connected to other lines are kept (endpoints within 0.5%): horizontal and vertical lines crossing into a grid; T-shaped lines that touch only one line in the grid; or at least 3 horizontal lines aligned left and right (tables with horizontal lines only; the lines of a grid and a separate horizontal line are joined only when the spacing is under 2 times the previous row, and two grids are not joined); a table nested inside a large frame is merged with the frame into one table. Separate horizontal lines (underlines under text, strikethroughs, dividers) do not enter a table and are not drawn as underlines. Two cells are merged when the line on their shared edge covers less than half of its length (not merged if the result is not a rectangle); a table without middle vertical lines is split into columns by text gaps (60% of rows are empty at the same place); in rows not covered by vertical lines, a cell is split into as many rows as it has lines of text (three-line tables, merged when a heading spans where the vertical lines did not reach); in a stretch covered by vertical lines with no horizontal line in between, it is split by line of text when there are at least 3 lines of text and more than half of the columns that have text have several of them (the body of a payslip or bill); when the header has vertical lines and the body below does not, columns follow the header; blocks with no text, or with only a horizontal line and no way to tell two columns, do not count as a table. Photos that were not enhanced have their lines searched at an angle by `findSkew`. Text lines are placed into cells by their center, and a line that spans a vertical line is cut by the CTC time steps of PP-OCRv6 (`@morph/tool-ocr` now also returns the approximate position of each character, with the model unchanged), and within one cell lines are joined into paragraphs per D-268; text outside tables is one line per paragraph, merged from the first column to the last column, with one blank row where the gap exceeds 1.5 times the line height. One grid for the whole page (benchmarked against CamScanner): the column lines of the tables (for tables with horizontal lines only, the columns split by gaps) that differ by less than 1% of the long side are aligned into columns shared by the whole page (two lines of the same table are not merged); each cell is converted to positions on the shared columns (spanning a column line that exists only in another table counts as a merge), with content and merge relations unchanged; a table starts from its own first column, column widths come from the shared columns, and inserting and deleting columns in the edit page apply to the whole page (every table it passes through changes, and a table keeps at least one column). Horizontal alignment is judged by the blank space between each line of text and the left and right edges of the cell (left, center, right, decided by the majority of lines; lines whose text fills the cell do not count), and text outside tables is judged by the left and right edges of the shared columns; when it cannot be told, amounts are right-aligned and everything else uses "General"; this is written into the xlsx `alignment horizontal` and the edit page. Numbers (`1,234.56`, `-5`, `12%`) are written as numbers, keeping the thousands separator, decimal places and percent sign, while values starting with 0, longer than 15 digits, or dates are written as text. The xlsx is written by our own code (fflate; sharedStrings, merges, column widths, row heights estimated from the number of lines, styles generated from borders / number format / alignment; sheet names cleaned, XML escaped, control characters removed). Pixels are decoded only once (PP-OCRv6's input size), shared by line finding and recognition; when there is an `ocrSource`, recognition is done on the pre-enhancement image and the boxes are converted per D-267. When `scope = tables` but no table is found on a page, that page is output as all content, and the result page says which pages. `RunItem.tableDoc { uri, for }` (same notation as `ocrSource`) points to the TableDoc in the run directory; the result page has "View and edit" under the xlsx (since D-366 this became "Put on the desk", edited in the file room, and `run/TableEditor.tsx` was deleted; it was `run/TableEditor.tsx`: column letters and row numbers, merged cells, tap to select and tap again to edit, showing this cell in the original image when selected, long-press on row numbers and column letters to insert and delete, recognition range, sheet tabs, undo and redo of 100 steps; once changed it is written as a new file and the old one is deleted; a page over 2000 cells is read-only). The built-in quick actions "Scan a table to Excel" and "Table picture to Excel" (language auto, not asked; flattening during scan is on by default per D-274). The new error `tableUnsupported` (the device cannot recognize this language; the text recognition pack gives text only and cannot be used). Evals XLS1, XLS2-en (built-in rules), PXLS1, PXLS2-en. In French, say classeur / grille, not tableau | Benchmarked against CamScanner's "table recognition": first build tables with lines (invoice line items, bank statements, printed forms) without adding a new model; in the screenshot CamScanner drew underlines as `____`. The table structure is kept by the TableDoc, the edit page changes it, and the xlsx is regenerated each time; the downloadable pack (layout and borderless-table models) will later be separate from `ppocr` | To be verified (the founder set the direction in conversation on 2026-10-28: first build tables with lines and tables with horizontal lines only, editing already in the first phase, the downloadable pack separate from ppocr, and separate horizontal lines do not count as table lines): unit tests (synthetic line drawings, fake recognition lines, unzipping the xlsx, TableDoc editing and undo) and `npm run check` pass; the Haiku evals XLS1, XLS2-en, PXLS1, PXLS2-en and the related TTS2-en, PTTS2-en, TR3, TR6, TX1 pass. | D-274 | **Scan flattening (UVDoc + refinement by text line)**: `scan.detect` gets a parameter `flatten` (omitted or true both mean on; the switch is "Flatten curved pages"; the built-in scan quick action writes `flatten: true`, old configs need no migration). After straightening (pages from the document camera too): pad the border with dark edges of 6% of the long side, scale to 488×712 and feed it to the UVDoc grid model (fp16, outputs only a 45×31 warp grid; the new native function `modelRun` runs it with ONNX Runtime, tensors go through temp files). When the text recognition model (`ppocr`) is installed, render a small image with a long side of 1280 according to UVDoc, use PP-OCRv6 det to find text lines, then find table lines: whole-page deskew (long lines and horizontal table lines take a length-weighted median, limited to ±0.5°, no rotation under 0.1°, no rotation when there is only one vertical line) + line-by-line straightening (sliding median + Gaussian smoothing, clamped after smoothing to within 2% of the long side, no refinement with fewer than 5 lines, vertical lines are also straightened when there are two or more); without `ppocr` it only flattens. The UVDoc grid, rotation and shift are combined into one triangle mesh, and Skia `drawVertices` resamples the straightened image only once (`flatten.ts` in `@morph/tool-image`). The model is a separate pack `dewarp` (15.9 MB), kept on our R2 (`morph-tools.stonetech.dev/packs/dewarp/1.0.0/`). License: the model card is Apache-2.0, the UVDoc code and the UVDoc and Doc3D datasets are all MIT, so a commercial app may distribute them, and LICENSE carries all the notices. | D-299 | **Everything a run needs to download is asked at once**: the first time the executor meets a step that needs a pack (after asking this step's parameters), it hands the packs needed by this step and later steps to the UI together (`ensurePacks`; later steps are estimated from the config's parameters and the current input, each pack listed once, and if any one step requires it, it is required). The UI lists only those not yet installed: one row each (name, size, purpose), the title gives the total size, and one "Download" downloads them all in order; optional ones (the flattening model, the text layer of a searchable PDF) have a checkbox, and if unchecked they are not downloaded and that step is still done; when there is a required one, "Cancel" does not run, and when all are optional it is "Don't download, continue". What was asked is not asked again: installed ones are skipped, and optional ones not downloaded are not asked again in this run (before, when two steps could both use the text recognition model, it asked twice). Missed estimates (another language chosen at run time) are asked separately when that step is reached. | D-323 | **Tapping on a widget**: what can be executed directly is only a button's "create an entry" (`create`) and the row action of each tile of tiles (`create` / `set` / `toggle` / `increment`). The tap does not open the app: on iOS it is an App Intent (`RunWidgetOp`), on Android a broadcast sent to itself, and both only write a file to `queue/` (operation, widget, record, fingerprint of the operation definition, time of the tap). The picture immediately switches to the one the app precomputed for "the same operation tapped k more times" (k ≤ 4, with "Noted" below the button); if several kinds were tapped mixed, 5 or more taps were made, or a day was crossed, it shows the original picture with "Updates after opening Morph" below. When the app starts, comes back to the foreground, or on Android when the app is open (`onQueue`), it takes the queue away and executes **by the time of the tap** ("today" is the day of the tap, and the record's creation time is also the time of the tap), in the same queue as the app's one-tap operations (`serial`), so the two sides never write at the same time; add/subtract and ticking are computed from the value stored at execution time (the same as tapping in the app), and create is always a new entry. It does not execute if the widget was deleted, the operation changed (fingerprint mismatch), the record is gone, the table is full, or the value cannot be saved. After executing, a banner pops up "Recorded n taps on the home-screen widget", and if some were not executed it says how many; one "Undo" reverts this whole batch. No banner on the widget and no undo there. Buttons that change a filtered set together (`setAll`, which must confirm first), open a form, or open a page, and list rows, open the corresponding page of the app when tapped (`morph://widget/<widget>`, `morph://record/<table>`). If the app crashes between taking the queue and executing, this batch is lost (never recorded twice) | The widget process cannot write the app's database (on iOS the database is not in the App Group), so all writing is left to the app and there is only one writer to conflict; using the time of the tap means opening the app late still records it on the right day | Decided; undo superseded by D-385 |

| D-326 | **Scan pack edge detection no longer takes a large table on the paper for the paper** (`scan.detect` on Android and Expo Go; for iOS see D-327): the scan pack page no longer gives only jscanify's largest contour but several candidates (jscanify's largest contour + the largest bright region: Otsu binarization, morphological closing, convex hull approximated to a quadrilateral; paper is usually brighter than the background) and a grayscale image with a long side of 500, from which `pickPaper` in the app (`@morph/tool-image`) picks: along each edge, measure the median brightness of a narrow strip on the inside and outside; if the outside is not below 80% of the inside, the paper continues past that edge; a candidate for which more than half of the measurable edges (those hugging the photo edge don't count) are like this is a frame on the paper and is discarded; of the rest, the largest is taken. When all candidates are taken for frames on the paper, the whole photo is returned (the paper fills the frame); when there were no candidates in the first place it still gives null, and the four-corner UI uses the inset default frame. The order of the four points the page gives is not fixed, and the app orders them with `orderQuad` | The founder's real-device test on 2026-10-29 (Android Samsung): a property-management bill with the paper almost filling the frame and a big table in the middle was found as the table's outer frame both times, and the only way was to tap "Whole photo" by hand. When the paper fills the frame the paper edge is not a closed contour, so jscanify taking the largest closed contour got the table frame. In Node, using the same page code + OpenCV.js on these 20 original images, with the four corners derived from CamScanner as the truth (IoU ≥ 0.85 counts as right): before the change 2 right (1 more right by chance with the default frame), 5 picked as an inner frame, 12 not found; after the change 17 right (5 of them the whole photo), with none of the previously right ones broken | To be verified: unit tests and `npm run check` pass; not seen on a simulator or real device. It can still go wrong: paper on a white cloth (takes the whole photo), a large shadow at a paper corner (the bright region cuts off a corner), no candidates at all (default frame as before) |

after straightening along the slope, lines are split, paragraphs are cut and positions are laid out, and stroke measurement, color and underlines are still taken from the original image; ② Tables without lines: several consecutive rows (a single-paragraph row sandwiched in between with a small gap is allowed) aligned by column, with almost no text in the white space between columns, at least three columns, three rows split into several segments, two rows using three or more columns, most text in the cells short (median no more than 24 characters), and column gaps no more than 3 line heights (farther apart means two blocks side by side, and D-332's "label: value" stays as is); when the upper and lower parts have different columns, the longest segment that can still form a table is taken; it is laid out as a table without borders (`DocTable.borderless`, no lines drawn in the docx or the edit page), cells record their position in the original image, and when most of a column is right-aligned the whole column is right-aligned; ③ Barcodes: several text-free horizontal lines from top to bottom all have many black-white alternations and line up in position (vertical bars), and are cropped as an image, and the scattered text recognized inside is discarded; | D-521 | **Convert to Excel writes font sizes and bold** (founder, in conversation, 2026-11-10; finding F3: `s-payslip-fr`). Sizes come from the line height the way Word does (`fontSizeOf`, 6 to 12 pt for body, up to 48 pt for text): the page gets a `bodySize`; a text block gets its own `size` when it differs from the page's by more than a quarter (short fragments never do); a table gets one size for all its cells (so numbers in a table stay consistent), written on the cells only when it differs from the page's by more than half a point. A photo taken at an angle makes long line boxes taller than the letters, so the estimate subtracts width times the page slope from every line height before comparing (Word does not, and is unchanged). Bold is the stroke thickness against the page's typical stroke (`strokeRatio` and `BOLD_RATIO` of Word), per text block and per table row: a row is bold when more than half of its filled cells look bold, so a short number misread as thick does not turn bold alone and a header keeps all its cells bold. The writer declares one font per size and weight (the 11 pt Calibri stays font 0, so a file without sizes is written exactly as before), sets row heights from the font size (a smaller font fits more characters per line), and the sheet view draws the size and weight. A text block also splits where two lines differ in height by 1.3 times or more, so a big title next to a small line is two blocks | The writer had one 11 pt font for every cell, so titles and fine print came out the same size | Done; tests fail on the old code (`sheet.test.ts`). Invariants: not touched. Config change: none; fixed code (the file format). Not seen on a simulator or a phone; the xlsx was rendered in LibreOffice on the Mac only |

Now the loose text is grouped the way Word groups it (`clusterLines` inside the layout model's regions, a line belongs to the smallest region that holds half of it, not Word's best-share rule, because the model often nests a big text region around small ones and the last line of a paragraph fell into the big one), and the blocks (text, pictures, found tables) go through Word's own side-by-side detection `arrangeUnits` (D-331). Blocks that sit beside each other form a `band`: they start on the same sheet row, each in its own column range; the band's column edges join the page's shared columns (D-272) so text and picture edges line up with table columns. Text in a band that sits beside a table or picture is merged over as many rows as it needs, so it never makes the neighbouring table rows tall. A single block in the right half of the page (a column heading above its column) starts at its own column instead of being centred across the whole sheet. Editing: inserting or deleting a sheet column moves or widens column-ranged text and pictures like tables (a block ending at the insertion point does not widen into it). Known limits: bands are found per group of overlapping rows as in Word, so a paragraph of a left column that has nothing beside it on the right is written full width; a ragged-right paragraph keeps the width of the page, not of its column | Two-column pages are common in CVs, papers and manuals; Word already had the detection, Excel only lacked somewhere to put the result | Done; tests fail on the old code (`sheet.test.ts`). | D-524 | **Convert to Word keeps a figure whose layout-model score is split over several classes** (an engineering fix from the 2026-11-10 converter-gaps assessment §4.1, not a decision by the founder). Cause: the layout model finds a chart or photo in the right place but spreads its score over image / chart / header_image on nearly the same box (for example chart 0.40 + image 0.35), and each class alone was below the 0.45 image cut-off, so scanned and digital pages lost their figure in Word. Rule: image-like detections (not seals) of 0.15 or more whose boxes overlap with IoU 0.7 or more are one figure; its score is the sum of the best score of each class, and it is kept at 0.45 or more. A figure kept only by this sum is marked `fused` and must have no recognized text inside it (no logo-text allowance, no diagram exception), because a wrongly kept image swallows its text out of the editable text. Two protections were fixed with it: a page-sized region (over half the page) no longer counts as the "duplicate" that removes the real figure inside it, and in `doc.ts` several small tables together covering over half of an image region also drop it (a form of one-table-per-field boxes was cropped as a picture on top of its own tables). The other `cleanRegions` protections (too much text, more than half the page, duplicates) are unchanged. Development documents, Word export: all 9 figure pages regain their figure (slides en/fr/zh and en scan/photo, report en/zh and en scan, academic fr), the two pages that already kept theirs keep them, no figure appears on the other synthetic pages except the ticked box on the AcroForm sample (a real glyph, no text lost), and the public documents gain only real photos and one signature. Holdout, run once after the rule was frozen: no new figure, one image fewer in one arXiv paper, and the three academic en pages still lack their figure. Layout rule only (`layout.ts`, one filter in `doc.ts`); no config or schema change; Excel untouched; not checked on the phone (PDF.js rendering, phone OCR); no invariant touched. |

Ordinary two-column prose and a field value's continuation retain the existing wrapping behavior (D-473). 2. The last column of a side-by-side row may borrow unused space to its right for a single-line left-aligned paragraph, budgeting the exported Arial font metrics, run sizes, first-line indent and cell padding; earlier column boundaries stay fixed, and the total remains within the content area (D-331). 3. Ordinary and nested tables use their source-relative horizontal offset as a Word table indent, bounded by the containing width, instead of discarding it (D-463). No sample IDs, names or document-type exceptions; no app config or sidecar format change. | The founder asked to fix the English invoice name wrapping, Chinese invoice issuer joining the date line, and English/Chinese/French receipt tables shifting left. The defects already existed in baseline 8696f88f; this supplements the existing reconstruction behavior rather than reverting the de7638e9 main update. | Decided; implemented with regression tests and verified exports. Native OCR and phone preview are not established by desktop rendering. |
| D-526 | **Word cell padding matches its text-width budget, and a short centered heading may use spare space in the last layout column** (engineering fix requested by the founder in this conversation on 2026-11-11: implement the first academic-layout repair group). Every ordinary, nested and layout table writes the same explicit 80-twip left and right cell margins used by the width calculation. D-525's last-column width allowance also accepts an explicitly marked centered heading whose source box fits one line at its exported size: it budgets runs, font size, indentation and padding, borrows only unused space to the right, leaves earlier column widths fixed and never exceeds the content width. Multiline headings, right-aligned headings and ordinary centered paragraphs retain their previous width path. No sample IDs or language exceptions. | Implicit table margins were rendered wider than the 4 pt per side assumed by the writer; tight table headers wrapped. Short Chinese headings also wrapped because their source ink boxes excluded the cell padding. This fixes export geometry; column ownership, alignment inference, paragraph grouping, picture filtering and photo style inference remain separate work. No config, migration or format change: OOXML serialization is fixed code. | Decided; regression tests fail on the old writer, the full check passes, and desktop exports plus a Hermes file-write/read probe are verified. No invariant touched; native OCR and phone Word preview remain unverified. |
| D-527 | **Non-dense Word pages keep proven prose columns continuous and infer alignment inside each column** (engineering fix requested by the founder in this conversation on 2026-11-11: implement the second academic-layout repair group). A two-column band with sufficiently wide cells and a multiline body paragraph establishes a scope. Compatible subsequent bands and isolated leaves retain their column; a spanning block, changed column boundary or substantial vertical gap ends the scope. Nearby leading fragments and compatible narrow heading bands can join that scope, while distant metadata and footers stay outside. Widths use the scope's content extents; source text, paragraph boundaries and non-alignment styles remain intact. Newly inferred paragraph alignment is recalculated against the proven column, retaining genuinely centered or right-aligned text. Sparse fields, one-column content and other column counts keep their prior path. The existing dense-page threshold (90 recognized lines) bypasses this new scope pass: larger layout tables interacted with heading keep-next pagination in two public tax-form probes, so dense-page pagination remains separate work. | Local vertical bands let isolated English/French body fragments become full-width paragraphs; page-relative alignment incorrectly centered right-column titles and mixed right/center alignment in references. This reuses DocRow version 1, with no new sidecar format, config or migration. Fixed reconstruction code is required because these are inferred document containers, not app UI choices. List-marker splitting, OCR-region paragraph ownership, figure filtering and photo style inference are unchanged. | Decided; implemented with regression tests that fail on the old builder, full validation and desktop/Hermes probes. No invariant touched; native OCR and phone Word preview remain unverified. |
